land.text: the seven taluks of the 19th-century Cochin State: Chittur, Cochin, Cranganore, Kanayannur, Mukundapuram, Trichur and Talapilly

successors.note: Disestablished 1 July 1949; merged with Travancore into Travancore-Cochin (the page says "1950" for the merger and "1949" for the end); Kerala formed 1 November 1956. travancore-cochin needs a dossier.

capitals.name: Perumpadappu / Vanneri
capitals.note: Perumpadappu near Ponnani was the headquarters; the capital was Vanneri (Chitrakooda) "from the beginning of the 12th century to the end of the 13th century".

capitals.name: Mahodayapuram (Kodungallur)
capitals.note: Moved here when the Zamorins attacked Vanneri in the later 13th century; the exact year is not given.

capitals.name: Cochin (Kochi)
capitals.note: "In 1405, Perumpadapu Swaroopam changed their capital from Mahodayapuram to Cochin" (an earlier section says 1341); the palace moved to Mattancherry in 1555, to Thrissur later and to Thripunithura around 1755.

rulers.name: Unniraman Koyikal II
rulers.note: The page gives only a partial ruler list, so the strip starts with 1503, the date of the first written dynastic records.

rulers.name: Rama Varma XVIII
rulers.note: Last official ruler, to 1964 on the page; he signed the 1949 accession agreement.

correction.text: Perumpadappu near Ponnani and Mahodayapuram, the early seats of the dynasty

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives no extent; "the kingdom had shrunk to its minimal extent" by the late 15th century. Perumpadappu (near Ponnani) and Mahodayapuram stand in for the early kingdom; it is a floor.

correction.text: the seven taluks of the 19th-century Cochin State: Chittur, Cochin, Cranganore, Kanayannur, Mukundapuram, Trichur and Talapilly

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cochin under Portuguese (1503-1663), Dutch (1663-1795) and British (1795-1858) overlordship. The seven-taluk table totals 1,362 sq mi (about 3,530 km2); the circles about Kochi, Thrissur and Chittur measure about 4,300 km2 (ratio 1.2). The 1753 loss of Karappuram and Alangad to Travancore is not subtracted from the circle shape.

region.text: Perumpadappu near Ponnani and Mahodayapuram, the early seats of the dynasty

ledger.note: Early 12th century: the Perumpadappu Swaroopam begins. The page says it "originated in the early part of the 12th century"; the first traditional ruler was Veera Kerala Varma. The 1102 date is not on the page; 1100 rounds "early 12th century".

1753: Kochi cedes Karappuram and Alangad. "In 1753, the tributary states of Kochi collectively known as Karappuram and Alangad were ceded to Travancore." Marthanda Varma allied with its ruler in 1757, "which enabled Kochi to survive".

region.text: the seven taluks of the 19th-century Cochin State: Chittur, Cochin, Cranganore, Kanayannur, Mukundapuram, Trichur and Talapilly

ledger.note: 1 July 1949: Cochin merges with Travancore. Disestablished 1 July 1949; merged with Travancore into Travancore-Cochin; Kerala formed 1 November 1956. "Cochin was the first princely state to willingly join the new Dominion of India in 1947."

wars.name: Calicut attacks on Cochin
wars.outcome: The Zamorin's assaults on Cochin were held off with Portuguese help (Battle of Cochin, 1504).
wars.note: The page names the Battle of Cochin (1504) and the Tirunavaya war without a territorial result.

wars.name: Mysore subjugation of Cochin

zones.text: Trichur (Thrissur), where the fort was captured in 1776

wars.outcome: Cochin accepted Mysore's suzerainty and paid tribute annually from 1766 to 1790; in August 1776 Cochin was invaded from the north and the fort at Trichur was captured.
wars.note: The Mysorean invasion page: "The king of Cochin accepted his suzerainty and paid him tribute annually from 1766 to 1790"; "In August 1776, Cochin was invaded from the north and the fort at Trichur was captured"; Cochin was asked to pay Rs. 400,000 and ten elephants in the 1774 operation (undated sentence). In 1788 "the king of Cochin refused and allied with Travancore" (undated). The page gives no occupation of Cochin by Tipu, no 1791 treaty, and names Cochin neither in the Treaty of Seringapatam nor for British paramountcy. The kingdom-of-mysore dossier should carry the vassal_start (1766) and vassal_end (1790) with counterpart kingdom-of-cochin. Shakthan Thampuran page: Rama Varma IX 1751-1805, ten tehsils (kovilakathum vathukkals) and two edavagas formed in the Kochi Kingdom in 1762, no territorial gain or loss.

certainty.note: The pages give taluks, towns and seats, never boundaries; the shapes are circles.

sources.title: Kingdom of Cochin
sources.note: Identity, capitals, seven taluks 1,362 sq mi, Portuguese 1503, Dutch 1663, British 6 May 1809, 1 July 1949.

sources.title: Marthanda Varma
sources.note: 1753: Karappuram and Alangad, tributary states of Kochi, ceded to Travancore; 1757 alliance of Marthanda Varma with Kochi.

sources.title: Mysorean invasion of Kerala
sources.note: Cochin paid Mysore tribute annually 1766-1790; August 1776 Cochin invaded from the north and the fort at Trichur captured; Cochin allied with Travancore against Tipu (1788); silent on any Tipu occupation of Cochin.

sources.title: Shakthan Thampuran
sources.note: Rama Varma IX of Cochin 1751-1805; ten tehsils and two edavagas formed in 1762; Thrissur as capital (undated); silent on Mysore, Zamorin and territory.

notes: Four pages opened (Kingdom of Cochin, Marthanda Varma, Mysorean invasion of Kerala, Shakthan Thampuran). The last two give the Mysore tribute (1766-1790) and the 1776 capture of the fort at Trichur and the 1762 tehsil reorganisation, and no boundary change; the Shakthan Thampuran page is silent on Mysore, the Zamorin and Palakkad. The Cochin page is thin on territory and dates: no 1102 founding, no 1753 cession, no 1761 or 1791 treaties, no 1766 tribute to Hyder Ali (it gives 1763 for the Mysore occupation of Cochin in context). The Portuguese protectorate (1503-1663; 27 September 1503 timber fort), Dutch alliance (1663-1795) and British paramountcy (confirmed 6 May 1809) are for portuguese-empire, british-empire (sa-06) to record as vassal events with counterpart kingdom-of-cochin. The 1814 Anglo-Dutch exchange ceded the islands of Kochi to the UK. Capital year of the move to Cochin is inconsistent on the page (1341 or 1405). Counterparts needing dossiers: travancore-cochin; Karappuram and Alangad (minor). The start year 1100 is a rounding of "early 12th century". Gazetteer lacks Chittur and Mahodayapuram as places; coordinates used.
